newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Talk subdued with diffs mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Talk subdued with diffs mixed.

text.p: U.S. spot product markets were subdued in early action Friday and did not look likely to heat up substantially as the day unfolded, traders said.
Differentials were mixed, weakening on New York Harbor gasoline and U.S. Gulf Coast low sulphur diesel, while firming on Gulf gasoline.
Differentials on other grades and in the midcontinent market were steady.
U.S. GULF
Gasoline markets in Houston were firmer early Friday amid talk of refiner buying, traders said.
But some players downplayed the signficance of the move, saying liquidity was poor enough for small deals to affect the market too easily.

Some players said prompt "M1" southern grade regular conven ional gasoline got done this morning at 2.85 cents under July futures -- nearly 0.75 cent firmer than on Thursday. But others, taking issue with such a firm number, said barrels had traded at a slightly weaker level of 3.10 cents under the July print.
"It's so quiet, it doesn't really mean much," said one trader.
In other action, low sulphur 74-grade diesel was heard, but not confirmed, done at 1.80 cents under July NYMEX -- a touch weaker than on Thursday.
NEW YORK HARBOR

New York Harbor M2 gasoline slipped on Friday amid continued concerns of ample supply. "This flies in the face of lesser imports but a lot of storage companies are still relatively full," said a Harbor gasoline trader.

M2 prompt unleaded differentials edged down about 15 points on Friday to -3.25/-3.00 cents to July NYMEX. A -3.00 cent deal was done late Thursday. Prompt A2 grade was traded at -0.25 cent to the print on Friday, with offers now heard at -0.35 cent.

Players said activity was light because many buyers were anticipating British Petroleum to sell off more of the about one million barrels of NYMEX reformulated unleaded gasoline it took delivery of earlier this month.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent products showed little price movement in early Friday action, traders said, though Group Three gasoline appeared to be holding gains made Thurdays from refinery buying interest, traders said.

Differentials for the prompt regular gasoline held steady with late Thursday levels, between 5.00 and 5.25 cents over the July NYMEX, while end of the month barrels were talked between 4.25 and 4.50 cents over the NYMEX.
Traders attributed Thursday's gains to the continued delays on the Houston-to-Tulsa-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline, which prompted some refiners to short cover on prompt commitments.
Market watchers said distillate activity remained very thin early Friday, with few players evident in the Chicago arena.
Unleaded gasoline firmed solidly Thursday afternoon in Group Three markets amid a spate of refiner buying, traders said.
